(def int-array "Creates an array of ints"
  (fn ([size-or-seq]
       (if (number? size-or-seq)
         (suss.bootstrap/packed-array 2 size-or-seq)
         (let [s (seq size-or-seq)
               a (suss.bootstrap/packed-array 2 (count s))]
           (loop [i 0 s s]
             (if s
               (do (suss.bootstrap/packed-store a i (first s))
                   (recur (inc i) (next s)))
               a)))))
      ([size init-val-or-seq]
       (let [a (suss.bootstrap/packed-array 2 size)
             n (alength a)]
         (if (number? init-val-or-seq)
           (loop [i 0]
             (if (< i n)
               (do (suss.bootstrap/packed-store a i init-val-or-seq)
                   (recur (inc i)))
               a))
           (loop [i 0 s (seq init-val-or-seq)]
             (if (and s (< i n))
               (do (suss.bootstrap/packed-store a i (first s))
                   (recur (inc i) (next s)))
               a)))))))
rationale: Clojure governs (ADR-0003, #336): an int array is a packed array of i32 elements, not a JS array. From a size it is zeroed; from a sequence, or with a fill value or sequence, each element is stored with the unchecked int cast, as Java's Number.intValue converts it, and a fill sequence stops at the size or its end. It mirrors the appendix's other packed constructors, which this early position cannot call.
